tb21_profile.skill: Infer an nn.Module class (a Transformer) from the keys and tensor shapes of a state_dict, load_state_dict into it, compute MSE on a dataset, then optimise only one layer with the rest frozen and serialise via TorchScript
tb21_profile.domain: PyTorch: state_dict introspection, nn.Module construction, torch.optim training loop, requires_grad freezing, torch.jit save/load
tb21_profile.task_form: recover/repair a lost definition from a persisted artifact, then optimise-to-a-budget (new MSE must beat the old) with a strict artifact contract

State dict will not load because the declared hidden size is wrong; read the weight shapes, fix the class, load, run eval-mode forward pass.
Deduce hidden layer sizes from weight shapes, repair SimpleMLP so weights.pth loads, then fit a second model and report metrics. Same two halves.
Reconstruct an undocumented PyTorch architecture from its saved state_dict and run a reproducible inference pipeline over a cleaned dataset.
arch.py is missing layer dimensions; infer the correct in/out channels so the state dictionary loads, then score every frame.
Full torch training loop: MSELoss, torch.optim.SGD, zero_grad/backward/step over parameters, report final loss. The tuning half of the TB task.
Saved state dict, model code lost; rebuild the MLP from the described shapes, load it and predict. Same recover-the-class-from-the-artifact move.
Original model code missing, only the .pth backup remains; reconstruct the architecture and run inference to regenerate embeddings.
Reconstruct the PyTorch MLP, load model_weights.pt, run a single batched forward pass and report aggregate outputs and timing.
Inference code lost but weights and vocab survive; reconstruct the model in PyTorch and recompute embeddings from the saved parameters.

Reason about how a model definition changed between two tagged versions and reconcile it with the live database. Structural-diff reasoning.
Initialise storage from a model definition and validate it against a written contract; make-code-and-artifact-agree, wrong stack entirely.

Train/validation split, linear-kernel training, prediction file with one label per line. Model-fitting workflow, no architecture recovery.
Install CPU PyTorch and run a distributed training example, verifying per-iteration loss appears. Same stack, only environment work.
Load a weights file plus its architecture config into a network and run inference. Weights-and-config-must-agree, but the library does the work.
Three-stage pipeline that trains SVR models, persists them, then estimates from a second scan; staged model artifacts across runs.
Train a scikit-learn classifier inside a pipeline and produce predictions; fit-then-predict only.
Fix a type-validation bug inside scikit-learn's neighbors module; debugging an ML library's internals, wrong framework and wrong genre.
Fetch a .pth model file intact rather than an HTML error page. Touches PyTorch artifacts but exercises nothing about their contents.

Reconstruct an undocumented PyTorch architecture from its saved state dict and drive it through a reproducible inference pipeline.
Hand-written torch training loop with MSELoss and torch.optim.SGD over specific parameters; the tune-weights-to-cut-MSE half of the TB task.

notes: TMax dominates because it contains a whole family of reconstruct-the-nn.Module-from-its-state_dict tasks, which is the TB2.1 crux; I ranked them by how much of the crux each covers (shape inference > load > train > serialise). TorchScript is almost absent from the pool: `torch.jit` matches exactly one document corpus-wide (pyg-8870), so that criterion has essentially one training source, which is why a SWE-Rebench issue reaches rank 4 despite the wrong genre. SWE-Smith reduces entirely to fvcore, the only PyTorch repository in that pool, so all ten entries are fvcore; that is honest rather than lazy, but downstream should know the diversity is nil. Recursive-Task-Synthesis is the weakest pool by far: four torch hits total, none about weights, so its defensible entries are recover-a-lost-model-definition-from-git tasks (SQLAlchemy, not PyTorch) scored on task_form. TerminalWorld has exactly one genuinely relevant task (tw_718060, which freezes a submodule); the rest are train-then-predict pipelines. The retrieval order surfaced a large block of generic ETL-plus-inference TMax tasks (task_008699, task_004636, task_008897) that share the phrase 'reconstruct the model' but give the architecture explicitly, so they teach nothing about reading a state dict; those were demoted.
